To find $\frac{dy}{dx}$, what other piece of information do you need?

options.text: The gradient at a particular x-value
The value of $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at a particular point
options.why: The second derivative is already supplied as a function of x.

questions.solution_text: Integrating gives $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4}{3}x^3+C$. A gradient at one particular x-value determines the constant $C$.
